title: Redwood + AuroraCloud reference-arch integration sync
summary: Technical sync to finalize reference architecture for AuroraCloud marketplace listing and joint solution. Covered deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), VPC networking, KMS integration, sizing, and a plan for a joint benchmark. Agreed next steps: share RA draft, run benchmark on Aurora dev cluster, and follow up on security artifacts.
next_steps: Maya to share reference architecture draft and diagram link (by 2026-05-07)
Diego to run initial throughput benchmark on Aurora dev cluster (by 2026-05-12)
Aurora to provide cluster specs and sample traffic profile (by 2026-05-10)
Schedule security deep-dive with Jamal and Redwood security (week of 2026-05-11)
action_items: Maya Chen - share RA draft + diagram link - 2026-05-07
Diego Ramos - run benchmark on Aurora dev cluster (CPU/GPU perf + quantized model) - 2026-05-12
Omar Nadeem - send VPC/subnet/topology + egress requirements - 2026-05-10
Jamal Reeves - gather SOC2/ISO checklist items and gaps - 2026-05-14
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:12] Lina Park: Lina here, platform PM at AuroraCloud. we've got Omar on infra, Sarah on solutions and Jamal on security.

[00:25] Maya Chen: Great. Diego from our infra team will run through the reference architecture and some performance numbers. um little note: doc link is in the invite - ref-arch v0.3 (see: https://redwood.ai/docs/ref-arch-auroracloud)

[01:05] Diego Ramos: cool, i'll share my screen - so this RA proposes three deployment patterns: 1) hosted API (redwood hosted), 2) dedicated reserved pools, 3) private VPC/on-prem. each has tradeoffs for latency/cost/data residency.
[02:20] Omar Nadeem: quick Q - for private VPC, how do you handle KMS? we need HSM-backed keys and BYOK for some customers.

[02:40] Priya Singh: yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations and we can do customer-managed keys; there's an HSM path for Private deployments, though there are some constraint notes around key rotation and cross-region replication.
[03:12] Jamal Reeves: also need to see audit logs retention, and can you push logs to our SIEM? we have strict retention rules for certain tenants.

[03:40] Diego Ramos: we expose audit logs and can integrate with S3 or a syslog endpoint, and we have an option to forward to a customer's Splunk/Datadog - will capture exact retention policies in the security doc.
[04:15] Sarah Kim: on marketplace listing - what metadata do you require? tile, icons, pricing sku, and any certs?

[04:33] Maya Chen: marketplace fields: listing name, short/long description, icons, categories, pricing tiers. For AuroraCloud we can propose a joint SKU for dedicated capacity and a pay-as-you-go option for hosted. We'll need logos and a one-page joint-solution summary.
[05:50] Lina Park: okay. For the RA itself, we need to ensure the network topology matches our marketplace onboarding templates - can you show the subnet nat/egress patterns?

[06:10] Diego Ramos: yeah - in the private pattern we recommend a two-tier subnet layout: inference nodes in private subnets, control plane (if customer-managed) in separate mgmt subnet, egress via NAT GW or VPC egress firewall. note: some words in the doc might say KV cache - that's the model KV cache for generation state, not a redis cache.
[07:02] Omar Nadeem: our ops team prefers minimal outbound egress; can Redwood run without egress to public internet?

[07:20] Priya Singh: yes, private on-prem or VPC deployments can be air-gapped with static artifact bundles. but hosted modes obviously need outbound for telemetry and model downloads unless you pre-stage images.

[08:05] Jamal Reeves: encryption at rest and in transit - TLS is fine, but we need to confirm that model artifacts and cache are encrypted with customer-managed keys. any limitations with quantized models?

[08:40] Diego Ramos: quantized models are just weights - encryption is orthogonal; we can encrypt disks and S3 artifacts with KMS. one caveat: if you use instance store for caching, ensure instance encryption config. we'll document the HSM flow.
[09:55] Sarah Kim: performance - what throughput can we expect for a 2k context using a g5-like GPU? do you have sample numbers?

[10:20] Diego Ramos: rough numbers: for a 2k context and a Llama-2 style model quantized to 4-bit, on a A100/p4 equivalent we see X tokens/sec in our internal bench - sorry speaker garble - i'll run a targeted benchmark on your dev cluster; we need your exact cluster spec.
[11:35] Omar Nadeem: i'll send the node types, network bandwidth and typical user QPS. we run a mix of short chat requests and longer generation. target latency SLO is p95 < 450ms for short gen.
[12:10] Maya Chen: that's helpful. for SLOs we can recommend a dedicated pool and automatic fallback to hosted during peaks; we should sketch the routing policy in the RA (cost vs latency tiers).
[13:30] Lina Park: question about billing metadata for marketplace - do you expose per-token usage or do we get aggregated billing?

[13:50] Priya Singh: we surface token-level breakdowns in the console and we can emit usage reports to the marketplace billing API. For dedicated contracts we support reserved capacity SKUs and monthly commit reporting.
[15:05] Jamal Reeves: can we do a SOC2/ISO artifact exchange? i'll need your control mappings and your pen-test schedule.
[15:30] Maya Chen: yes - we'll share a compliance packet and our SOC2 report; Diego will follow up with security team to coordinate a dedicated deep-dive.

[16:10] Sarah Kim: podcast - sorry, i mean point - for the RA diagram, can you include a simplified Terraform snippet for the VPC peering and route tables? our infra team prefers infra-as-code examples.
[16:34] Diego Ramos: absolutely, we'll add a minimal terraform example and also a k8s helm chart snippet for the private helm installation. note: some customers prefer operator-based installs.
[17:50] Lina Park: any blockers we should know about for marketplace certification?

[18:05] Maya Chen: the usual: security artifacts, a joint one-pager, and marketplace listing assets. also need to run a short bake/benchmark and a joint press blurb if you want co-marketing. nothing blocking tech-wise.
[19:20] Omar Nadeem: can Redwood handle network egress costs if we use hosted fallback?
[19:40] Priya Singh: we typically bill for egress where applicable; we can model options - in a joint SKU we can absorb some costs for co-sell pilots, but it'll be in the pricing proposal.

[20:55] Diego Ramos: next step: i'll spin up a small perf test on your dev cluster with a quantized 13B model - need ssh/credentials or a test harness. Omar - can you provide access or run the harness?
[21:20] Omar Nadeem: we'll run the harness internally and share logs. i'll also include top-of-stack metrics (cpu/gpu, mem, net).
[22:10] Jamal Reeves: schedule a security-only call. prefer the week of May 11th.
[22:30] Maya Chen: noted. i'll send calendar invites and share the RA draft by Friday. any final Qs?
[22:45] Lina Park: no, thank you - excited to move forward. agreed on the next steps and the benchmark.
[22:55] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and invites. meeting adjourned.
